r0.why: Magnitude and direction, directed segment in Euclidean space, alternative names from [23],[24],[29].

r1.why: Latin 'carrier', carrying A to B, magnitude/direction, equivalence class of same-length same-direction segments from [1],[3],[32].

r2.why: Not located at a place, velocity/acceleration/forces, arrows for non-distances, scalars have no direction from [6],[8],[33],[34].

r3.why: Analogous operations and laws qualify them as vector-space example; pure-math definition from [4],[5],[25],[26].

r4.why: Mid-19th-century systems, Grassmann 1840 neglected until 1870s, Clifford, Gibbs 1881 from [12],[13],[14],[18],[19],[21].

r5.why: Coordinate dependence, R^n with dot product, isomorphism motivating standard from [9],[39],[40],[43],[44].
